prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key policy proposals (2015 manifesto)

Economy and public finances
- Raise the personal allowance to at least £13,000; remove income tax from minimum-wage earnings; lift 40% threshold to £55,000; add a 30% band; abolish inheritance tax; increase transferable allowance for couples.
- Cut small business rates by 20% for properties with rateable value under £50,000.
- Reduce deficit via: leaving the EU to save net contributions; lower overseas aid to 0.2% of GNI over three years; scrap HS2; replace the Barnett Formula with a needs-based system; cut the cost of government and quangos.
- Clamp down on multinational tax avoidance and review diverted profits measures.

Immigration and borders
- Leave the EU to control free movement; introduce an Australian-style points system.
- Five-year moratorium on unskilled immigration; limit highly skilled work visas to 50,000.
- Create five visa types (work, visitor, student, family reunion, asylum); require private health insurance for most temporary migrants.
- No access to most benefits or non-urgent NHS care until five years of contributions.
- No amnesty for illegal immigration; faster removals; revoke visas for foreign offenders; allow settled EU residents to remain post-referendum.

Health and social care
- Invest an extra £12bn over five years in the NHS; recruit 8,000 GPs, 20,000 nurses, 3,000 midwives; pilot GPs in A&E; free hospital parking.
- Increase mental health and dementia funding; parity of esteem; expand liaison services.
- Tackle health tourism by requiring insurance for non-eligible patients.
- Create a statutory “licence to manage”; replace national regulators with locally elected county health boards; end PFI use; seek changes to EU directives affecting training and trials; exclude the NHS from TTIP.
- Increase social care funding by £1.2bn annually (phased); integrate health and social care under the NHS; improve carers’ pay and support; set a Dignity Code; improve home care standards; explore a fracking-funded sovereign wealth fund for future care costs.

Welfare, pensions, families
- Abolish the “bedroom tax”; retain housing benefit for under-25s; pay HB directly to landlords on request.
- Replace outsourced disability assessments with GP/specialist-led processes; increase carers’ allowance; fund advisers in foodbanks.
- Flexible state pension window (earlier, reduced option); expand free, independent pension guidance; criminalise pension cold-calling; restore war widows’ pensions for life.

Education and childcare
- Abolish Key Stage 1 SATs; reduce teacher workload; cap class sizes with an aim to reduce further.
- Expand grammar, vocational and technical schools; late transfer options; restore GCSE maths tiers; make first aid part of PSHE; reform Ofsted; protect special schools.
- Waive tuition fees for UK students studying STEMM/Medicine who work in the UK for five years; reduce places until graduate jobs expand; treat international students separately in migration stats.
- Maintain 15 free hours early-years care; reform vouchers to allow vetted informal carers; increase nursery places via planning; require wraparound care 8am–6pm in primaries; emergency childcare registers.
- Shared parenting presumption; reform care and adoption processes.

Housing and environment
- Bring empty homes back into use; national brownfield register, remediation support and tax incentives; target one million brownfield homes by 2025.
- National Homeless Register; prioritize social housing for those with five years of tax/NI; reinvest Right to Buy proceeds; restrict RTB/Help to Buy to citizens (with armed forces exceptions).
- Protect green belt and prime agricultural land; strengthen local control via referenda; support small village developments; allow inheritable mortgages.

Transport
- Cancel HS2; consider South East capacity with options including re-opening Manston; restrict speed cameras to safety use; phase out road tolls; oppose road-pricing tech mandates.
- Scrap the DCPC for HGV drivers; adjust HGV levies to target foreign vehicles; VED exemption for vehicles over 25 years old.

Energy
- Repeal the Climate Change Act; end subsidies for new onshore wind and large-scale solar; support hydro; develop shale gas with safeguards and community benefit; support coal with CCS; remove green levies from bills; leave the EU ETS.

Employment and small business
- Allow employers to prioritize citizens; enforce minimum wage; code for zero-hours contracts (no exclusivity, notice and pay guarantees, path to secure contracts).
- Tackle late payments via HMRC sanctions; pilot trade credit insurance; 30 minutes free town-centre parking; simplify procurement for SMEs; reduce regulatory burdens.

Farming, food, animal welfare, fishing
- Replace CAP with a capped Single Farm Payment per acre, with premiums for organic/rare breeds; support dairy and sheep sectors; review labelling; support GM research with a free vote.
- Tougher sentences and lifetime bans for animal cruelty; CCTV in abattoirs; regulate religious slaughter; ban live exports; support small abattoirs.
- Leave the CFP; create a 12-mile zone and 200-mile EEZ; rebuild stocks with no-take zones; curb destructive methods; fairer quotas for under-10m boats; ensure angling representation.

Crime, justice, political reform
- Increase Border Agency staff (+2,500) and 3,500 frontline police/prison posts; new UK Bill of Rights; leave EU justice measures like the European Arrest Warrant.
- Rationalize constabularies; invest in tech; update sentencing for cyber, trafficking, domestic abuse; reduce FOBT stakes to £2; decriminalize TV licence non-payment; expand prison capacity; education and victim compensation; deport foreign offenders with appeals from abroad.
- Citizens’ initiative referendums; robust recall; open primaries; select committee confirmation and spending veto powers; proportional voting with constituency link; tighten postal voting; merge oversight bodies.

Trade, defence, foreign aid, EU exit
- Leave the EU; regain WTO seat; seek a UK–EU free-trade agreement and cooperation on security, health and agencies; create a Post‑EU Secretariat.
- Defence: meet and exceed 2% of GDP by 2020 (+£4bn); retain nuclear deterrent; deploy carriers, review aircraft choice; unify intelligence under a Director; income tax exemption while on operational duty; oppose any EU army.
- Overseas aid: reduce to 0.2% of GNI over three years, focusing on emergency relief, vaccinations, water/sanitation; close DFID and merge functions into the Foreign Office; prefer UK delivery where compliant; promote “trade not aid.”
